answer: Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. Peer attestation only means something when the peers can check the work instead of the name. The walnut holds work receipts rather than names, so the ridge of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the dune of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, converted to a slow vesting stream.
